correctness.rationale: With fixed denominator M>=2 and coprime numerators, Carvalho's exact order-class recurrence gives (M-z phi(M))F_M=1+z sum_{1<d<M, d|M}phi(d)F_d. For M=p^s m with p largest prime, the only divisors whose phi(d)/d equals rho=(p-1)/p are powers p^j. By induction on divisors, modulo functions holomorphic at z0=p/(p-1), F_{p^j e} is congruent to F_{p^j}, and the totient identity sum_{e|m}phi(e)=m collapses all pole principal parts to the prime-power F_{p^s}=p^{-s}(1-rho z)^{-s}. The multiplier M-z phi(M) is nonzero at z0 for m>1; all other possible poles have modulus >=1/eta_M>1/rho. This justifies the coefficient error O_M(n^{tau(M)} eta_M^n), leading polynomial-binomial term, and tail factor 1/(1-rho)=p; density of infinite orders zero is cited rather than assumed pointwise. Independently rebuilt the rational-function recurrence using SymPy and checked cancellation for all M=2..90, and directly iterated T using exact rational arithmetic over one modulus period for M=3,4,6,10,12 and orders 1..3. The infinite proof is divisor induction, not finite experiment.

value.rationale: Fixed-denominator stopping statistics for a natural rational map are motivated by the open individual finite-order question. The theorem gives a sharp general asymptotic with both leading constant and polynomial factor, and proves a nonobvious dominance/cancellation by the largest prime-power component. It is not a routine restatement of density one or a small computational improvement; all lower prime factors contribute only exponentially smaller terms.

limitations: Fixed denominator M before n->infinity; not a uniform-in-M estimate.
No claim that every rational has finite stopping order.
Finite checks were corroborations; proof relies on the published exact-order recurrence.
